title: Caesar Salad
subtitle: Grilled chicken, parmesan and anchovy dressing
excerpt: Thinly sliced grilled chicken breast served over crisp pan-fried croutons with a sharp, creamy anchovy dressing made from scratch. The dressing uses a single egg yolk emulsified with olive oil and lemon, which comes together quickly and tastes far better than anything from a bottle. Anchovies melt into the dressing and provide salt rather than fishiness.
sourceNotes: Caesar salad was created in 1924 by Caesar Cardini, an Italian immigrant running a restaurant in Tijuana, Mexico; he improvised the dish on a busy Fourth of July weekend using ingredients he had on hand.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The dressing can be made up to 2 days ahead and kept covered in the fridge. Give it a good stir before using.

content.text: The dressing is an emulsion of egg yolk, olive oil, lemon juice and anchovies. Whisk the yolk with lemon juice and crushed garlic first, then drizzle in the olive oil very slowly while whisking continuously. If you rush the oil in, the emulsion breaks and you get a greasy puddle rather than a creamy sauce. Pan-fried panko croutons cook in 3 minutes and stay crunchier longer than oven-baked versions.

items.prepNote: approx 2 breasts, sliced thin and griddled or pan-fried
plus extra for cooking the chicken and croutons

content.text: Make the dressing: whisk together the egg yolk, Dijon mustard, lemon juice, crushed garlic and chopped anchovies in a bowl until combined. Slowly drizzle in the olive oil while whisking constantly until the dressing is thick and creamy. Season with pepper (anchovies provide plenty of salt). Add a splash of cold water if the dressing is too thick.

Season the chicken breasts and slice each one horizontally into two thin escalopes. Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a frying pan over a high heat and cook the chicken for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden and cooked through. Rest for 2 minutes, then slice thinly.

In the same pan, heat another drizzle of oil over a medium-high heat. Add the panko breadcrumbs with a pinch of salt and toss constantly for 2 to 3 minutes until golden and crisp. Tip out onto a plate.

Toss the dressing through the salad leaves (or serve without leaves as a grain-free option). Top with the sliced chicken, crispy panko croutons and a generous shower of grated parmesan. Finish with a squeeze of lemon and black pepper.

items.symptom: Dressing has split and looks oily
items.cause: Oil was added too quickly before the previous addition had emulsified
items.fix: Start a fresh yolk in a clean bowl, then slowly whisk the broken dressing into it as if it were the oil. This usually rescues it completely.

items.cause: Anchovies are naturally very salty and parmesan adds more
items.fix: Dilute with an extra squeeze of lemon and a teaspoon of cold water. Taste before adding any extra salt to this dish.
